Instructions

Answer the following questions and/or complete the exercises in RMarkdown. Please embed all of your code and push the final work to your repository. Your report should be organized, clean, and run free from errors. Remember, you must remove the # for any included code chunks to run.

Load the tidyverse

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Data

For this assignment, we will use data from a study on vertebrate community composition and impacts from defaunation in Gabon, Africa. One thing to notice is that the data include 24 separate transects. Each transect represents a path through different forest management areas.

Reference: Koerner SE, Poulsen JR, Blanchard EJ, Okouyi J, Clark CJ. Vertebrate community composition and diversity declines along a defaunation gradient radiating from rural villages in Gabon. Journal of Applied Ecology. 2016. A description of the variables is included inside the data folder.

1. Load IvindoData_DryadVersion.csv and store it as a new object called gabon.

gabon <- read_csv("data/IvindoData_DryadVersion.csv")

3. Clean the data as necessary following the conventions from lab 6.

gabon_new <- gabon %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(across(where(is.character), tolower))

4. Use mutate() Change the variables HuntCat, LandUse, and TransectID to factors. Be sure to store the output as a new dataframe and use it for the remaining questions.

gabon_newest <- gabon_new %>% 
  mutate(across(c(hunt_cat, land_use, transect_id), as.factor))

5. Make a plot that shows the number of transects for each land use type.

gabon_newest %>% 
  select(land_use) %>% 
   ggplot(mapping=aes(x=land_use))+
  geom_bar(mapping=aes(fill=land_use))+
  labs(title="# transects for each land use type")

6. How does vegetation richness compare among land use types?

gabon_newest %>% 
  select(veg_rich, land_use) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=land_use, y=veg_rich))+
  geom_boxplot(mapping=aes(fill=land_use))+
  labs(title="vegetation richness vs. land use type")

National parks have the highest median vegetation richness, while certain logging concessions have higher vegetation richness overall. Neither has the lowest vegetation richness.

7. For which land use type (national parks, logging, or neither) is average all species diversity the greatest?

names(gabon_newest)
##  [1] "transect_id"              "distance"                
##  [3] "hunt_cat"                 "num_households"          
##  [5] "land_use"                 "veg_rich"                
##  [7] "veg_stems"                "veg_liana"               
##  [9] "veg_dbh"                  "veg_canopy"              
## [11] "veg_understory"           "ra_apes"                 
## [13] "ra_birds"                 "ra_elephant"             
## [15] "ra_monkeys"               "ra_rodent"               
## [17] "ra_ungulate"              "rich_all_species"        
## [19] "evenness_all_species"     "diversity_all_species"   
## [21] "rich_bird_species"        "evenness_bird_species"   
## [23] "diversity_bird_species"   "rich_mammal_species"     
## [25] "evenness_mammal_species"  "diversity_mammal_species"
gabon_park <- gabon_newest %>% 
  select(land_use, diversity_all_species) %>% 
  filter(land_use=="park")

  mean(gabon_park$diversity_all_species)
## [1] 2.425143
gabon_logging <- gabon_newest %>% 
  select(land_use, diversity_all_species) %>% 
  filter(land_use=="logging")

  mean(gabon_logging$diversity_all_species)
## [1] 2.232538
gabon_neither <- gabon_newest %>% 
  select(land_use, diversity_all_species) %>% 
  filter(land_use=="neither")

  mean(gabon_neither$diversity_all_species)
## [1] 2.3575

The average all species diversity is highest for national parks.

8. Is there a relationship between vegetation richness and mammal species richness?

gabon_newest %>% 
  select(veg_rich, rich_mammal_species) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=veg_rich, y=rich_mammal_species))+
  geom_point(mapping=aes(color=veg_rich))+
  geom_smooth(method=lm, se=T)+
  labs(title="mammal species richness vs. vegetation richness")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

There appears to be somewhat of a positive relationship between vegetation richness and mammal species richness.

9. Use filter to find all transects that have greater than 15 tree species or a breast height diameter between 50 and 60cm.

  filter(veg_rich>15 | between(veg_dbh, 50, 60))
